c.tagline: Alpine lake city of diplomacy, watchmaking, and the soaring Jet d'Eau.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are among Europe's highest and always metered; book by app or use a rank rather than hailing on the street, and expect airport, luggage, and night surcharges.

emergency.note: 112 is the general European emergency number and reaches police, fire, and ambulance; 117 is direct police and 144 is the ambulance service.

avoid.reason: The Pâquis district near the main station has street drug dealing and petty theft late at night, and pickpockets work the lakefront in summer.

hood_desc: Geneva's medieval heart on the hill, a maze of cobbled lanes around St. Pierre Cathedral, Place du Bourg-de-Four, antique shops, and art galleries; best for first-timers who want history, sights, and atmosphere within walking distance.

The lively, cosmopolitan lakeside quarter behind the main station, packed with international restaurants, bars, and the famous Bains des Pâquis bathing pier; a walkable, sometimes gritty base for nightlife and cheaper eats close to everything.

An elegant left-bank residential district running along the lake from the Jardin Anglais past the new Eaux-Vives harbour and beach, with parks, boutiques, and a relaxed waterfront feel; good for travellers who want calm, greenery, and lake views.

A charming, Sardinian-built 'village' just south of the centre with pastel low-rise houses, leafy squares, artisan workshops, indie boutiques, and buzzing cafe-bar terraces; suits those after a bohemian, creative atmosphere away from the tourist core.

A student and alternative district around the huge Plaine de Plainpalais, home to the university, the twice-weekly flea market, farmers' markets, cinemas, and a young, arty going-out scene; great for budget travellers and market lovers.
lodging: The Ritz-Carlton Hotel de la Paix

water.note: Tap water is excellent Alpine-sourced and safe to drink everywhere.

transit.hours: Trams, trolleybuses, and buses run roughly 5:00 AM to around midnight; on Friday and Saturday nights the Noctambus network covers the late hours.
transit.pay: One unireso ticket covers TPG trams and buses, the Mouettes lake shuttles, and Léman Express and regional trains within the zone. A full 'tout Genève' 60-minute ticket is about CHF 3.00 (~US$3.40) and a short-hop 'saut de puce' about CHF 2.00; a day card is around CHF 8-10. Buy from machines at every stop or in the TPG or Léman Express apps. Guests of any Geneva hotel or hostel receive a free Geneva Transport Card covering all public transport for the length of their stay, and arriving air passengers get a free 80-minute ticket from a machine in baggage claim.

tip.r: Service is included by law, so tipping is not expected; rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service is appreciated.
